title: A Second Language Is More Than Words: How It Rewires Your Brain
title_zh: 第二语言远不止于词语：它如何重塑我们的大脑
intro_zh: 本文约950词，适合CET-4水平。通过科学研究例子，说明外语学习在认知、健康和社交方面的长期益处。

paragraphs.en: On a Monday morning, two new employees sit in a global company. One opens an email written in Spanish and replies confidently in a few minutes. The other must wait for translation software just to understand a short product description in Chinese. Everyone can see the practical advantage of being bilingual. But the influence of language study goes far beyond such office moments. In recent decades, brain research has shown that learning a second language creates new connections between neurons, and those changes improve our ability to focus, make decisions, and even control our emotions.
paragraphs.zh: 周一早晨，在一家全球公司里，两名新员工坐在一起。一人收到一封西班牙语邮件，几分钟内就自信地回复了。另一人却只能等翻译软件去理解一份简短的中文产品说明。任何人都能看出掌握双语的现实优势。但是，语言学习的影响远不止这些办公室时刻。近几十年来，大脑研究表明，学习第二语言会在神经元之间建立新的连接，这些改变会提升我们的专注力、决策力，甚至情绪控制能力。

paragraphs.en: One of the strongest findings is that bilingual speakers are better at tasks that require attention switching and self-control. Psychologists call this set of skills the executive function. In a classic card test, people are asked to sort cards first by shape and then by color. Bilingual participants change rules faster and make fewer mistakes than people who speak only one language. Why? Because every time bilinguals open their mouths, both languages are active in the brain, and the mind must choose the correct one while suppressing the other. This process is like doing mental push-ups. After years of practice, the control centers of the brain become stronger, so daily mental challenges feel easier.
paragraphs.zh: 一个最有说服力的发现是，双语者在需要注意力转换和自我控制的任务中表现更好。心理学家把这组能力称为执行功能。在一个经典卡片测试中，受试者先按形状、再按颜色分类卡片。双语受试者比只说一种语言的人切换规则更快、错误更少。为什么？因为双语者每次开口时，两种语言都在大脑中活跃着，大脑必须选出正确的语言并抑制另一种语言。这个过程就像做脑力俯卧撑。经过多年操练，大脑控制中心变得更强，日常的心智挑战也就显得更轻松。

paragraphs.en: The most impressive proof may come from studies of old age. Millions of older people worry about dementia, a disease that destroys memory and clear thinking. In Toronto, scientists studied elderly patients in memory clinics and found that bilingual patients first showed symptoms four or five years later than monolingual patients. In another long-term British project, researchers followed 835 people from the age of 11 to over 70. Those who learned a second language, even in middle age, kept sharper memories and scored better in reading tests. The brain seems to use language practice as a kind of savings account: an extra route around damaged areas. Therefore, picking up a new language in adulthood is not a waste of time; it is an insurance for the future mind.
paragraphs.zh: 最令人印象深刻的证据或许来自对老年的研究。数百万老年人担心痴呆症——一种破坏记忆和清晰思维的疾病。在多伦多，科学家研究了记忆门诊的老年患者，发现双语患者的症状比单语患者晚出现四到五年。在另一项英国长期项目中，研究者从11岁到70多岁追踪了835人。那些在中年甚至更晚学习第二语言的人，保持了更敏锐的记忆力，并在阅读测试中得分更高。大脑似乎将语言练习当作一种储蓄账户：为受损区域提供一条额外线路。因此，成年后学习一门新语言并不是浪费时间，而是为未来的大脑购买保险。

paragraphs.en: Languages also open the door to fresh perception of reality. Russian speakers have separate names for light blue and dark blue; as a result, they are faster at telling apart these subtle color differences. Also, members of the Kuuk Thaayorre community in northern Australia say ‘north’ or ‘south’ instead of ‘left’ or ‘right.’ Because their language forces them to keep track of directions, they always know where north is, even inside unfamiliar buildings. When they learn another language such as English, this unusual ability becomes much weaker. These examples suggest that language is not a simple list of labels. It trains the senses to choose certain details. Every new language gives you another lens, allowing you to see aspects of the world that had been invisible before.
paragraphs.zh: 语言也为我们打开了对现实的全新感知。俄语使用者分别用不同词表示浅蓝和深蓝，因此他们能更快地分辨这些细微色差。在澳大利亚北部的库克泰约雷人社区，人们不说“左”或“右”，只说“北”“南”“东”“西”。由于语言迫使他们注意方向，他们即使在陌生的室内也总能知道北方在哪里。而当他们学了英语等另一种语言后，这种特殊能力会明显减弱。这些例子说明，语言并非简单的标签清单；它训练我们的感官去选择某些细节。每多学一门新语言，就多了一副镜头，让你看见以前看不见的世界面貌。

paragraphs.en: Such mental skills would be valuable enough, but language learning also changes how we relate to other people. Imagine traveling in a village where few people speak English. If you have learned ten local phrases, greetings become gifts. A market seller may invite you to taste fruit; an elderly person may tell you a story. These welcoming moments seldom happen for someone who relies only on translation apps. In addition, repeated struggles with grammar and vocabulary develop empathy. Once you know how it feels to search for a word, you become patient with foreigners who speak your language incorrectly. You pay less attention to an imperfect accent and more attention to the meaning behind their words. In this way, each language learner becomes a more generous listener and a warmer companion.
paragraphs.zh: 这类心智能力已经十分宝贵，但语言学习同样改变我们与他人相处的方式。想象你到一个很少有人会说英语的村庄旅行。如果你学了十句当地话，问候就成了礼物。集市摊主可能邀你尝水果，老人可能给你讲个故事。这些温暖时刻很少会发生在只依赖翻译软件的人身上。此外，反复与语法和词汇作斗争会培养同理心。一旦你知道找不到词是什么感受，你对母语说得不地道的外国朋友就会更有耐心。你更少注意不完美的口音，而更多注意对方言语背后的含义。这样，每个语言学习者都会变成更宽容的倾听者和更温暖的伙伴。

paragraphs.en: All these cognitive and social benefits send a strong signal to employers. Global companies need people who can solve problems in more than one cultural context. Economic surveys from many countries confirm that employees who use a foreign language at work often earn between 10 and 20 percent more than those who do not. Bilingual engineers, nurses, and customer-service managers can serve larger groups of clients, understand medical histories in the original language, and make fewer mistakes in international teamwork. Perhaps more importantly, an adult who succeeds in learning a language shows discipline, curiosity, and openness - exactly the qualities that are hardest to teach. Consequently, a language on a resume is more than decoration; it is evidence of a flexible mind.
paragraphs.zh: 所有这些认知与社交优势都会向雇主发出强烈的信号。全球化公司需要能在不止一种文化情境中解决问题的人。许多国家的经济调查证实，工作中使用外语的员工收入通常比不使用外语的人高10%到20%。掌握双语的工程师、护士和客户服务经理能为更多客户服务，可用原语言读懂病历，并在国际团队协作中减少差错。也许更重要的是，能在成年后学好一门语言的人，表现出了自律、好奇心和开放态度——这些恰恰是难以教会的品质。因此，简历上的一门外语不只是装饰，它是有弹性思维的证据。

paragraphs.en: Adults sometimes believe that language learning must start in childhood to truly work. That belief is contradicted by brain science: the brain stays plastic throughout life. In the Edinburgh study, older adults attending evening classes saw improvement in attention after just four weeks. The best method is to attach language to something you already love - your favorite songs, sports news, cooking programs, or video games. Use new words when you talk to yourself; change your phone menu to the target language; write one short sentence each day. Such small repeated actions are enough to build a new map in the brain. Perfection does not matter; progress does. After a few months, learners are often surprised to find they can catch the general meaning of an article or a film scene without opening a dictionary.
paragraphs.zh: 成年人有时认为，语言学习必须在童年开始才真正有效。这种信念被脑科学推翻：大脑终生保持着可塑性。在爱丁堡研究中，上夜校的老年人在仅仅四周后就表现出注意力改善。最好的方法，是把语言和你本来就爱的事物联系在一起——你喜欢的歌曲、体育新闻、烹饪节目或电子游戏。自言自语时用上新词；把手机菜单设成目标语言；每天写一个短句。这样的小小重复足以在大脑中搭建新地图。完美并不重要，进步才是。几个月后，学习者往往会惊讶地发现，不用打开词典就能大致理解一篇文章或一段电影台词了。

paragraphs.en: In an age of instant translation, why not simply press a button? Because translation converts words, not understanding. A machine will never explain why an apology in Japanese often begins with a statement rather than a simple ‘sorry.’ It will not tell you how old idioms echo in someone's heart or why humor varies from culture to culture. Learning a foreign tongue is, finally, a way of becoming more completely human. It keeps the brain busy, the senses sharp, and the heart open. Therefore, choose a language that interests you, leave perfectionism behind, and let the new world inside you grow.
paragraphs.zh: 在即时翻译的时代，为什么不直接按一下按钮呢？因为翻译转换的是词语，而不是理解。机器不会向你解释，为什么日语的道歉往往以一句陈述句开头，而不是简单的“对不起”；也不会告诉你古老习语在某人心中有多少回响，或幽默为何因文化而不同。学习一门外语，归根结底是成为更完整的人的一种途径。它让大脑保持忙碌、感官保持敏锐、内心保持开放。所以，选一门你感兴趣的语言，放下完美主义，让新世界在内心生长吧。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Translation software will soon replace the need for human language learning.
Learning a foreign language brings benefits to the brain, social life, and career.
Bilingual people are smarter than monolingual people in every test.
Language learning should begin in childhood to be effective.
questions.explain: 文章从大脑、社交、职业等方面说明学习外语的多种益处；A与最后一段观点相反，C过于绝对，D与第七段矛盾。

questions.q: Why did bilingual patients show symptoms of dementia later than monolingual patients in the Toronto study?
options: They had more years of schooling.
Their brains had extra pathways to deal with damage.
They could speak to doctors in two languages.
They exercised more than the monolingual group.
questions.explain: 文章第三段提到双语患者能更晚出现症状，因为大脑将语言练习当作储蓄账户，提供“绕开受损区域”的额外线路，对应认知储备。

questions.q: What does the example of the Kuuk Thaayorre suggest about language?
options: People in isolated communities are born with an excellent sense of direction.
The vocabulary we use can affect where we direct our attention.
English speakers are slower at learning to use maps.
Direction language is impossible to learn unless you live in Australia.
questions.explain: 库克泰约雷人因日常用语强制使用东南西北，才一直保持方向感；这说明语言能训练注意力与感知。A过度归因于天生，C、D文中未提及。

questions.q: The phrase “cognitive and social benefits” in Paragraph 6 probably refers to ______.
options: improvements in thinking abilities and in relating to people
advantages in earning money and traveling cheaply
changes in physical health and daily diet
skills in operating computers and translation software
questions.explain: cognitive 意为“认知的”，social 意为“社交的”，结合上下文指的是思维能力和人际交往方面的好处。
